fact.text: In 1880, James A. Garfield was elected US president in what is still the closest American presidential race by popular-vote margin.

lithuania.headline: „Valstietis“ Gaižauskas ragina premjerą trauktis dėl plagiato disertacijoje
lithuania.summary: Valdančiosios LVŽS frakcijos narys Dainius Gaižauskas sako, kad premjeras Mindaugas Sinkevičius turi atsistatydinti, net jei tai reikštų pirmalaikius rinkimus, nes toks elgesys mažina pasitikėjimą valdžia. Premjeras pažeidimus pripažino, bet teigia nekvestionuojantis darbo mokslinės vertės.
lithuania.context: ISM Vadybos ir ekonomikos universiteto Etikos komisija premjero disertacijoje nustatė reikšmingų citavimo ir šaltinių priskyrimo pažeidimų, įskaitant plagiato atvejus. Komisija laipsnio naikinti nesiūlė, bet įpareigojo darbą ištaisyti per pusmetį.

lithuania.headline: Prezidento patarėjas: 5 proc. BVP gynybai – tik minimumas
lithuania.summary: Kitų metų biudžeto projekte gynybai numatyta daugiau kaip 4,8 mlrd. eurų, arba 5 proc. BVP – mažiau nei šiemet skirti 5,38 proc.; prezidento patarėjas Deividas Matulionis sako, kad pirkimai gali vėluoti, bet tikslo iki 2030 m. sukurti sausumos diviziją neatsisakoma. Valstybės kontrolierė skaičiuoja, kad planams reikėtų 5,44 proc. BVP, o liberalų lyderė Viktorija Čmilytė-Nielsen teigia, kad „nuodėmių mokesčiai“ biudžeto neišgelbės.
lithuania.context: Po Rusijos invazijos į Ukrainą 2022 m. Lietuva sparčiai didino išlaidas gynybai, iki tol joms skirtas palyginti mažas. Šiemet skirta 5,38 proc. BVP, tačiau rengiant 2027 m. biudžetą lėšų trūksta, ir Vyriausybė Seimui pateikė projektą su 5 proc. BVP. Prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda pripažino, kad to nepakanka.

lithuania.headline: Nuo lapkričio 1 d. – mokestis siuntoms iš „Temu“, nauji KET ir Darbo kodekso reikalavimai
lithuania.summary: Nuo sekmadienio už pirkinius iš „Temu“ ar „AliExpress“ reikia papildomai mokėti, įsigaliojo vairuotojams svarbūs KET pakeitimai, o pakeistas Darbo kodeksas didina delspinigius ir ilgina bandomąjį laikotarpį daugiau uždirbantiems. Pokyčiai įsigaliojo ir pacientams.

world.headline: Michigan Democrat backs Republican on eve of US midterms
world.summary: Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost Michigan's Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival Mike Rogers a day before Tuesday's midterms; her long-time chief of staff quit and Trump invited her to join the Republican Party. Polls show Democrats leading or tied in seven battleground governor races, while Trump made a final campaign push in states Republicans won before.
world.context: Tuesday's midterm elections decide control of Congress halfway through Trump's second term, and polls have predicted Democratic gains. Michigan's Senate race is one of the most fiercely contested, and Stevens and El-Sayed fell out mainly over support for Israel.

world.headline: Nine killed as business jet nosedives onto Florida road
world.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin to the Bahamas plunged almost vertically onto a busy road in Palm Beach County on Sunday, killing all nine on board; the pilot radioed that the plane was descending at 20,000 feet per minute. No one on the ground was reported hurt, but 600 nearby residents were evacuated.
world.context: The crash site is about 14 km from Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort; the NTSB is investigating.

world.headline: Iotova becomes Bulgaria's first elected female president
world.summary: Iliana Iotova, an ally of Prime Minister Rumen Radev who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won Sunday's runoff with about 51-52% of the vote against pro-Western-backed banker Andrey Gyurov, exit polls showed.
world.context: Iotova was already serving as president, having succeeded Radev, now prime minister. The post is largely ceremonial.

world.headline: UN ends Western Sahara peacekeeping mission after 35 years
world.summary: The UN's MINURSO mission expired on Sunday after Russia vetoed a US resolution backed by 11 of 15 Security Council members that would have made Morocco's autonomy plan the only basis for talks. Guterres warned of the risk of renewed hostilities.
world.context: Morocco has claimed Western Sahara since Spain withdrew in 1975, while the Algeria-backed Polisario Front seeks an independent Sahrawi state. The UN set up MINURSO in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on the territory's future, which never took place.

interesting.headline: Antonelli becomes F1's youngest world champion
interesting.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli clinched the title at 20 years and 68 days by finishing third in Mexico City behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record by more than three years. He is the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

interesting.headline: Claude Code's game-clone limits snag legitimate projects
interesting.summary: Restrictions in Anthropic's Claude Code meant to stop it from building clones of existing games are also blocking legitimate game projects, developers say.
interesting.context: Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding assistant.

interesting.headline: 'Godzilla Minus Zero' thrills Tokyo before Japan release
interesting.summary: Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to 'Godzilla Minus One' sold out two screenings as the Tokyo International Film Festival's centrepiece ahead of its 3 November Japanese release; set in 1949, it brings in King Ghidorah and holds 92% on Rotten Tomatoes.
interesting.context: 'Godzilla Minus One' (2023) was the first Godzilla film to win an Oscar, for visual effects.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: The six-day Kherson truce ended on Sunday night with no violations reported after Russia rejected Kyiv's offer to extend it; nearly 800 people were evacuated from Oleshky. Hackers then sent fake alerts, including nuclear threat warnings, through Ukraine's air raid app, and Russia's emergency app was also hit.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Ukraine pushed Russian forces back from Kyiv and later Kherson city, but the front has barely moved since 2023. Trump has pressed both sides for a deal, and a local truce around Oleshky, mediated by Melania Trump with the Pope's involvement, began last Tuesday.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers exploded after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, as Qatar-mediated indirect talks on releasing more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could reopen the strait, ran into a third day. Trump said the US may at some point have to hit Iran with a 'sledgehammer'.
ongoing.context: Tensions over Iran's nuclear programme led Israel and the US to strike Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025. In February 2026 the US and Israel went to war with Iran, which hit US bases across the region and closed the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route. Qatar now mediates indirect talks on reopening it.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: France reported more than 770 arrests on Saturday, half the previous week's number, and Paris prosecutors opened an attempted-murder probe after a petrol bomb set a gendarme alight. Rioters injured more than 100 police in Frankfurt, and French pupils' groups say school blockades resume on Monday.
ongoing.context: Youth-led protests began in France in late September over the high cost of living and poor public services, especially schools. On 17 October some 2,600 people were arrested and up to 3,000 shops looted. This autumn the protests spread to Germany, Portugal, Switzerland and other countries.

ongoing.title: Israeli operation in the West Bank
ongoing.update: Israeli forces withdrew from Hebron on Monday after a 10-day siege, the city's governor said; more than 3,300 Palestinians were displaced or affected and 15 homes and other structures demolished.
ongoing.context: Israel occupied the West Bank in 1967 and has stepped up raids there since the Gaza war began in October 2023. The Hebron siege started on 23 October after two Palestinians shot dead two Israeli soldiers.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: The UN migration agency says more than 300,000 people have fled their homes in western Yemen, almost all in the past two months, as fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces intensifies.
ongoing.context: Yemen's war began in 2014 when Iran-backed Houthi rebels seized the capital Sanaa; a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015. After four years of relative calm, fighting reignited in July amid the wider Middle East conflict, and the Houthis launched an offensive in the west in September.
